subject: Biology SL
title: Biology SL Paper 2 Section A Mock v1

questions.subject: Biology SL
questions.question: An investigation measured catalase activity at different hydrogen peroxide concentrations. Answer all parts using the data.

parts.label: (a)
parts.question: Calculate the percentage increase in reaction rate from 1.0 to 2.0% hydrogen peroxide.
markscheme: Increase = 5.4 − 3.2 = 2.2 arbitrary units min⁻¹.
Percentage increase = 2.2 ÷ 3.2 × 100 ≈ 68.8% (accept 69%).
markschemeJa: 増加量＝5.4－3.2＝2.2 任意単位 min⁻¹。
parts.modelAnswer: The rate increases by 2.2 units, which is about 69%.
parts.modelAnswerJa: 速度は2.2単位増加し、約69%の増加です。

parts.label: (b)
parts.question: Describe the relationship between substrate concentration and reaction rate.
markscheme: Reaction rate increases as hydrogen peroxide concentration rises from 0.5 to about 4.0%.
The increase becomes smaller at high concentrations and the rate approaches a plateau.
markschemeJa: 過酸化水素濃度が0.5%から約4.0%へ上がると反応速度は増加する。
高濃度では増加幅が小さくなり、反応速度は頭打ちに近づく。
parts.modelAnswer: The rate rises with substrate concentration but gradually approaches a maximum.
parts.modelAnswerJa: 基質濃度とともに速度は上昇しますが、次第に最大値へ近づきます。

parts.label: (c)
parts.question: Explain why the reaction rate approaches a maximum at high substrate concentration.
markscheme: At high substrate concentration, most catalase active sites are occupied for much of the time.
Enzyme concentration becomes limiting, so extra substrate produces little further increase in rate.
markschemeJa: 高基質濃度では、多くのカタラーゼ活性部位がほぼ常に占有される。
酵素濃度が制限要因となり、基質をさらに増やしても速度はほとんど上昇しない。
parts.modelAnswer: At high substrate concentration catalase becomes saturated, so the amount of enzyme limits the maximum rate.
parts.modelAnswerJa: 高基質濃度ではカタラーゼが飽和し、酵素量が最大速度を制限します。

parts.label: (d)
parts.question: A student claims that 4.0% hydrogen peroxide is the optimum substrate concentration. Evaluate this claim using the data.
markscheme: The measured rate at 4.0% is high and close to the highest measured value.
The rate at 6.0% is slightly higher, so 4.0% is not proven to be the concentration giving the absolute maximum.
More concentrations and replicates around 4–6% would be needed before identifying an optimum reliably.
markschemeJa: 4.0%での測定速度は高く、測定された最大値に近い。
6.0%ではわずかに高い速度なので、4.0%が絶対的最大を与える濃度とは証明されていない。
最適値を信頼して判断するには4〜6%付近でより多くの濃度と反復測定が必要である。
parts.modelAnswer: The data show a near-plateau by 4.0%, but 6.0% is slightly higher. Therefore 4.0% cannot be identified confidently as the optimum without more measurements and replication.
parts.modelAnswerJa: 4.0%付近で頭打ちに近いものの6.0%がやや高いため、追加の濃度と反復なしには4.0%を最適濃度と断定できません。

parts.label: (e)
parts.question: Suggest three improvements that would increase the reliability or validity of the investigation.
markscheme: Use several replicates at each substrate concentration and calculate a mean.
Keep temperature, pH and enzyme concentration constant between treatments.
Use smaller substrate-concentration intervals near the plateau / measure reaction rate with a calibrated quantitative method.
markschemeJa: 各基質濃度で複数回反復し平均値を求める。
処理間で温度、pH、酵素濃度を一定にする。
頭打ち付近で基質濃度の間隔を小さくする／校正された定量的方法で反応速度を測る。
parts.modelAnswer: Replicate each treatment and calculate means, control temperature/pH/enzyme concentration, and use finer substrate intervals near the plateau with a quantitative measurement method.
parts.modelAnswerJa: 各条件を反復して平均を求め、温度・pH・酵素濃度を統制し、頭打ち付近ではより細かな濃度間隔と定量測定を使います。

stimulus.title: Catalase activity at different substrate concentrations
stimulus.description: Equal catalase samples were tested at constant temperature and pH.
stimulus.note: Each value is the mean of three trials.

questions.subject: Biology SL
questions.question: Electron micrographs were used to compare two cell types.

parts.label: (a)
parts.question: Identify which cell type is most likely prokaryotic.
markscheme: Cell type P.
markschemeJa: 細胞型P。

parts.label: (b)
parts.question: Explain your identification using two features in the table.
markscheme: Cell P lacks a nucleus / membrane-bound nucleus.
Cell P has 70S ribosomes and no mitochondria, both consistent with a prokaryotic cell.
markschemeJa: Pには核／膜で囲まれた核がない。
Pには70Sリボソームがありミトコンドリアがなく、原核細胞の特徴と一致する。
parts.modelAnswer: P is prokaryotic because it lacks a nucleus and mitochondria and contains 70S ribosomes.
parts.modelAnswerJa: Pは核とミトコンドリアを欠き、70Sリボソームをもつため原核細胞です。

parts.label: (c)
parts.question: Explain how compartmentalization can benefit cell type Q.
markscheme: Membrane-bound organelles create different internal environments for different reactions.
Compartmentalization can concentrate enzymes/substrates and separate incompatible processes, increasing efficiency or control.
markschemeJa: 膜で囲まれたオルガネラは異なる反応に適した内部環境をつくる。
酵素や基質を局所的に濃縮し、両立しない反応を分離して効率や調節を高められる。
parts.modelAnswer: Compartmentalization separates reactions into specialized environments, allowing better control and efficient concentration of enzymes and substrates.
parts.modelAnswerJa: 区画化により反応を適した環境に分け、酵素や基質を集中させて効率よく制御できます。

questions.subject: Biology SL
questions.question: Plant tissue was placed in sucrose solutions of different concentrations.

parts.label: (a)
parts.question: Estimate the concentration at which there is no net change in tissue mass.
markscheme: Approximately 0.35 mol dm⁻³ (accept 0.3–0.4 mol dm⁻³).

parts.label: (b)
parts.question: Explain why tissue gains mass at 0.10 mol dm⁻³.
markscheme: The external solution has a higher water potential than the cell contents.
Water enters cells by osmosis across partially permeable membranes, increasing tissue mass.
markschemeJa: 外液は細胞内より水ポテンシャルが高い。
水が部分透過性膜を通って浸透により細胞内へ入り、組織質量が増える。
parts.modelAnswer: Water enters the cells by osmosis from the higher-water-potential solution, increasing mass.
parts.modelAnswerJa: より高い水ポテンシャルの溶液から浸透で水が細胞へ入り、質量が増えます。

parts.label: (c)
parts.question: Suggest one variable that should be controlled.
markscheme: Any valid variable such as temperature, immersion time, tissue dimensions, solution volume or tissue source.
markschemeJa: 温度、浸漬時間、組織サイズ、溶液量、組織由来など適切な変数。
parts.modelAnswer: For example, keep immersion time constant.
parts.modelAnswerJa: 例えば浸漬時間を一定にします。

parts.label: (d)
parts.question: Explain why several tissue samples should be used at each concentration.
markscheme: Replicates reduce the influence of anomalous samples / random variation.
A mean can be calculated, improving reliability of the estimated trend.
markschemeJa: 反復により異常値やランダム変動の影響を小さくできる。
平均値を求められ、傾向の信頼性が高まる。
parts.modelAnswer: Replicates reduce random variation and allow a mean to be calculated, making the result more reliable.
parts.modelAnswerJa: 反復によりランダム変動を減らし平均を求められるため、結果の信頼性が高まります。

questions.subject: Biology SL
questions.question: A heterozygous plant was self-crossed for a gene with complete dominance.

parts.label: (a)
parts.question: Calculate the expected number of recessive offspring among 240 offspring.

parts.label: (b)
parts.question: Explain how meiosis and fertilization produce the expected 3:1 phenotype ratio.
markscheme: The two alleles segregate during meiosis so each gamete receives one allele.
Random fertilization gives an expected genotype ratio of 1 homozygous dominant : 2 heterozygous : 1 homozygous recessive.
With complete dominance the first two genotypes show the dominant phenotype, giving 3 dominant : 1 recessive.
markschemeJa: 減数分裂で2つの対立遺伝子が分離し各配偶子は1つを受け取る。
ランダム受精により遺伝子型比は期待上1優性ホモ:2ヘテロ:1劣性ホモとなる。
完全優性では最初の2遺伝子型が優性表現型となり3:1になる。
parts.modelAnswer: Alleles segregate into gametes and random fertilization produces a 1:2:1 genotype ratio, which becomes 3:1 phenotypically because the dominant allele masks the recessive allele in heterozygotes.
parts.modelAnswerJa: 対立遺伝子が配偶子へ分離し、ランダム受精で1:2:1の遺伝子型比となり、完全優性により表現型は3:1になります。

parts.label: (c)
parts.question: Suggest why an observed ratio may not be exactly 3:1.
markscheme: Random sampling variation / chance in fertilization, especially with a finite sample size.
markschemeJa: 有限の標本ではランダムな受精・標本変動があるため。
parts.modelAnswer: Random sampling variation can cause the observed ratio to differ from the expected value.
parts.modelAnswerJa: ランダムな標本変動により観察比は期待値からずれることがあります。

questions.subject: Biology SL
questions.question: Allele R increases resistance to an insecticide. Its frequency was measured across generations.

parts.label: (a)
parts.question: Describe the change in allele R frequency.
markscheme: Allele R frequency increases over successive generations.
It rises from 0.10 at generation 0 to 0.68 at generation 16.
markschemeJa: R頻度は世代とともに上昇する。
0世代の0.10から16世代の0.68へ増加する。
parts.modelAnswerJa: Rは0.10から0.68へ継続的に増加します。

parts.label: (b)
parts.question: Explain how natural selection can cause this change.
markscheme: Heritable variation in insecticide resistance exists in the population.
Insecticide exposure gives resistant individuals higher survival/reproductive success than susceptible individuals.
Resistant survivors contribute more R alleles to later generations, increasing allele frequency.
markschemeJa: 耐性に関する遺伝可能な変異が集団内に存在する。
殺虫剤下では耐性個体の生存・繁殖成功が感受性個体より高い。
耐性個体が次世代へより多くRを伝え、頻度が上昇する。
parts.modelAnswer: The insecticide acts as a selection pressure. Resistant individuals survive and reproduce more, so R becomes more common.
parts.modelAnswerJa: 殺虫剤が選択圧となり、耐性個体がより多く生存・繁殖するためRが増えます。

parts.label: (c)
parts.question: Distinguish natural selection from the idea that the insecticide causes organisms to develop resistance because they need it.
markscheme: Selection changes frequencies of existing/heritable variants; it does not direct mutations according to need.
markschemeJa: 自然選択は既存の遺伝的変異の頻度を変えるのであり、必要に応じて突然変異を方向づけるわけではない。
parts.modelAnswer: Natural selection favors heritable variants already present or arising randomly; the insecticide does not create needed mutations.
parts.modelAnswerJa: 自然選択は既存またはランダムに生じた遺伝的変異を選び、必要に応じて突然変異を起こすわけではありません。
